About Diabetic Neuropathy 
 Diabetic neuropathy consists of two words diabetes + neuropathy. Neuropathy means dysfunction of the one or more peripheral nerves. Diabetic neuropathy means the neuropathy caused due to the high sugar level in the body. It mainly affects the nerves of foot and legs. It is one of the major complication of the diabetes.

sections.sign_and_symptoms_of_peripheral_neuropat:
Numbness and tingling sensation. 
 Burning sensation. 
 Severe pain and cramps. 
 Loss of balance and coordination. 
 Muscle weakness. 
 Foot problems like ulcers, sores and severe deformities. 

 2. AUTONOMIC NEUROPATHY: Autonomic neuropathy occurs when there is a damage to the nerves that manages the day to day functions such as blood pressure, heart rate, sweating, bowel and bladder functions and digestion.

 It affects the ability to regulate the body temperature. 
 Difficulty in pupil accommodation. 

 3. RADICULOPLEXUS NEUROPATHY: It affects mainly the nerves in the thighs, buttocks and hips. It’s commonly seen in patient with type 2 diabetes.
sections.sign_and_symptoms_of_the_radiculoplexus_:
Sudden, severe pain in the buttocks and thighs. 
 Difficulty rising from the sitting position. 
 Weak muscles. 
 Pain in abdomen if it got affected. 

 4. MONONEUROPATHY: Mononeuropathy it is called focal neuropathy. It affects the specific nerve. The nerve may be in face, torso or legs. 
 Signs and Symptoms depend on which nerve is affected. Few signs and symptoms are as follows: 

 Bell’s palsy (Paralysis of the one side of face). 
 Pain in thigh. 
 Pain in the foot. 
 Pain in the lower back. 

 Mononeuropathy causes severe pain, but it does not cause long term problem. It mainly affects the older adults.
sections.the_causes_of_the_diabetic_neuropathy_ar:
High blood sugar level causes damage to the nerves and weakens their ability to transmit signals ,along with that it also weakens the walls of the capillaries which supply them oxygen and nutrients. 
 Inflammation of the nerves. 
 Genetic factors: Some genes are prone to nerve damage. 
 Excessive use of alcohol and smoking: It narrows and hardens the arteries and blood vessels, reducing the blood flow to the legs and foot. It makes difficult to wound heal and damage the integrity of the blood vessels.
sections.risk_factors_for_diabetic_neuropathy:
Bad control of sugar level. 
 Obesity. 
 Kidney disease. 
 Chronic diabetes.
sections.complications_of_diabetic_neuropathy:
Amputation of the limb: Due to nerve damage, one may loss the sensation of feeling in the leg. Sores and ulcers remain unnoticed due to diabetes blood flow decreases to the legs, hence chances of infection increases. The infection may lead to the bones, and at last there is a formation of the gangrene. It is impossible to treat and require amputation of the limb. 
 Urinary Problems: Urinary problems like Urinary tract infection and incontinence may occur due to the damage of the nerves which controls the urinary bladder functions. Proper functioning of the urinary bladder does not take place, hence chances of infection increases. 
 Digestive Problems: Nerve damage of the digestive system may leads to problems like diarrhea, constipation, bloating and loss of appetite. 
 Sexual Dysfunction: Due to the damage to the nerve supply to the sex organs. It causes erectile dysfunction in males and dryness in the vagina, libido in females.
